newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish audit office sees '97 deficit 38 bln SKR.
newsitem.headline: Swedish audit office sees '97 deficit 38 bln SKR.

text.p: Sweden's National Audit Office forecast on Thursday that the state's budget deficit for 1997 would be 38 billion crowns.
The office said this forecast did not include the sale of the state's slice of Nordbanken.
The forecast deficit is an improvement of one billion crowns compared to a previous forecast made last December.
The office said it was a 17 billion crowns improvement to the approved central government budget deficit.
It noted that from the start of 1997 the central government budget deficit and the central government borrowing requirement are identical.
"The improvement compared to the central government budget is both due to a decrease in total expenditures and an increase in total revenue," the office said in a statement.
Total expenditure was forecast 670.3 billion crowns compared to the central government budget's calculation of 677.8 billion crowns.

Revenue for 1997 was forecast by the office at 632.7 billion crowns which was 7.5 billion crowns higher than the office's December forecast and 9.3 billion crowns more than the central government budget.

"The decrease in total expenditure is assigned to interest on national debt and National Debt Office net lending while the increase in total revenue is mostly explained by a sale of shares in Stadshypotek (7.6 billion crowns)," the statement said.
